article.title: America, Satan Called and He Wants His Baby Brother Back
article.author: Desi Cortez
article.content: The opinions expressed here are solely the author's and do not reflect the opinions or beliefs of the LA Progressive. Stephen Miller is a hate monger; he promotes racism and hostility, and he is the pillar of the MAGA world who’s pulling Trump’s strings in the White House I’d venture to guess the Devil understated their relationship. Stephen Miller could be Lucifer’s identical twin, separated at birth, raised among mortals, and dispatched to Washington to finish what Hell couldn't accomplish alone. I’m serious! Something wicked this way comes In my opinion, Miller is among the most ominous, creepy, dangerous, morally repugnant figures to emerge from the Land of MAGA. His hostility toward immigrants , fixation on who belongs, and apparent indifference to suffering remind me less of an American statesman than Joseph Goebbels, Adolf Hitler’s propaganda minister, who transformed prejudice into Nazi patriotism, lies into doctrine, and persecution into public duty. Different century, different uniform, but the political echoes are unmistakable. I’m not saying history repeats itself word for word. Related: Goebbels’s Ghost and Miller’s Dream of a “Unified Reich” But I sure as hell hear it rhyming. Those echoes should make grown Americans sick to their stomachs. We have seen what happens when government first teaches its people whom to despise. This modern merchant of misery now occupies corridors where Abraham Lincoln struggled to preserve an imperfect Union, and Franklin Roosevelt confronted fascism, including the homegrown sympathies of prominent Americans like Henry Ford and Charles Lindbergh. Here’s what should scare the living hell out of anybody with a functioning conscience: I don’t believe Donald Trump is the mastermind of this nightmare. I believe Stephen Miller is. Remember Pinky and the Brain , those laboratory rats endlessly plotting world domination? Miller is the Brain, the calculating schemer who knows how to exploit power. Trump is Pinky, or Orangie, the loudmouthed accomplice who mistakes his mountainous ego for intelligence. Orangie believes he’s issuing orders while the Brain quietly drafts instructions. Trump supplies the spectacle, presidential seal, and vanity. Miller supplies the ideology, targets, and calculated cruelty . It’s a bargain between a man addicted to applause and another addicted to the machinery of power. That’s what makes this frightening. Trump’s hatred is theatrical. Miller’s is methodical. Trump bellows about enemies; Miller helps build machinery to pursue them. Trump wants applause; Miller wants policies that outlive the cheering mob. One is a political arsonist. The other studies blueprints, deciding which exits to lock before the fire starts. On November 6, Trump named Miller White House chief of staff, effective November 9. The man I suspect writes the instructions will now supervise the staff. Apparently, political arson earns a promotion. What haunts me isn’t simply what Miller has said or done. It’s what further barbarities a man with his convictions might pursue when handed extraordinary power, surrounded by obedient officials, and protected by a president whose moral compass points permanently toward himself. Congress and the press ought to be on this fellow’s tail like bloodhounds tracking a stolen ham. May the gods have mercy on America. The most dangerous man in the White House may not sit behind the Resolute Desk. He may stand beside it, whispering into the president’s ear, plotting who belongs in America and who should suffer for believing they do. Seven episodes explain why I refuse to mistake Miller’s influence for ordinary corporate Republican conservatism. The White Nationalist Reading Club In 2015 and 2016, Miller emailed Breitbart editors material from VDARE, a website associated with white nationalism. He recommended The Camp of the Saints , a novel portraying nonwhite refugees overrunning Western civilization. Imagine choosing bedtime reading from the white supremacist bargain bin, then helping write immigration policy for a nation of immigrants. His defenders can debate his intentions; the emails establish what he circulated. Bigotry doesn’t become harmless by acquiring a government email address. Nor does a poisonous worldview become respectable because somebody types it into a memorandum and calls it policy. The Confederate Flag Sympathy Department After white supremacist Dylann Roof slaughtered nine Black worshippers inside Charleston’s Mother Emanuel AME Church in 2015, officers reportedly bought their captured killer Burger King. Heaven forbid the poor little mass murderer should go hungry. Nine innocent people lay dead in their church, yet someone made sure the killer got a meal. Ain’t that a bitch?! Meanwhile, retailers began removing Confederate merchandise, and Miller’s leaked emails showed him pushing back by comparing that merchandise with communist products still sold in stores. Consider the level of Vulcan inability to “feel,” the moral bankruptcy: Nine Black people were murdered while worshipping God, and Miller was busy defending the commercial dignity of Confederate symbols. What a talent for locating the wounded feelings of a flag… while grieving families remain inconveniently human. Apparently Confederate merchandise deserves a more passionate defense than Black humanity. Am I lying? The Muslim Ban Salesman Miller helped craft Trump’s first administration’s travel restrictions affecting predominantly Muslim countries. The administration called it national security; the courts fought over successive versions, and the Supreme Court upheld a revised one in 2018. Miller insisted the revisions preserved the underlying policy. When “religious discrimination” is the accusation, changing the wrapping paper doesn’t end the argument. Apparently, Lady Liberty needed a bouncer, and Miller volunteered, knocking folks down to get the opportunity, the privilege to inspect the guest list. 4. The Child Separation Accountant. In 2018, the administration’s zero-tolerance policy separated thousands of migrant children from parents. Miller defended the approach as simple. Simple! That describes choosing coffee or tea, not a terrified child crying for a mother vanished behind federal procedures. Officials called it enforcing immigration law. Families experienced government hands reaching across a parent’s arms and taking a child away. If that doesn’t chill your blood, check your pulse. Children don’t give a damn about presidential approval ratings. They want their mothers, their fathers, their homes. The American-Only Preacher At Trump’s October 2024 Madison Square Garden rally, Miller declared, “America is for Americans and Americans only.” On a discount flag, that might pass for patriotism. Amid speeches portraying migrants as threats, it resurrected America’s poisonous question: Who counts as American? A nation built by Indigenous peoples, enslaved Africans, and immigrants hardly needs another government official handing out certificates of belonging according to his preferred bloodlines and cultural tastes. The Three Thousand Arrests Man In 2025, Miller pushed ICE toward 3,000 arrests daily , according to Reuters and Axios. Not 3,000 dangerous criminals specifically. Three thousand arrests. Numbers. Quotas. Human beings reduced to production targets, as though deportation were a warehouse chasing quarterly bonuses. Officials say enforcement protects public safety. But when the scoreboard becomes the mission, justice and arithmetic start looking suspiciously interchangeable. You don’t have to be a genius to recognize the danger when liberty becomes a numbers game. The Birthright Citizenship Undertaker Miller championed Trump’s attempt to restrict birthright citizenship for children born on American soil. After the Supreme Court rejected that effort in June 2026, he complained that any interpretation requiring a nation to “suicide your civilization” must be wrong. Imagine that: newborn babies reclassified as threats to civilization , the Constitution treated as an irritating suggestion, and citizenship discussed like country-club membership controlled by inherited privilege. Fourteenth Amendment? Apparently, to Miller, fourteen is just an unlucky number. Seven Questions That Ought to Make Washington Sweat Now, after weighing this record, I have seven questions for investigators and a federal grand jury. Not seven convictions. Seven questions. I want the files opened, the witnesses sworn, and the facts dragged into daylight. If nothing criminal happened, establish that. If laws were broken, let the evidence point toward the guilty, however expensive their suits. Let us be clear about the stakes. This is not a demand that prosecutors manufacture a case to satisfy my temper. It is a demand that powerful men answer questions ordinary citizens never get to dodge, with lawyers present, records preserved, and excuses stripped of their polished Washington wrapping. Not exactly an unreasonable request. Who had their rights trampled? Were people unlawfully detained, mistreated, or punished, and did Miller knowingly help make it happen? An official title isn’t a magic shield, and the presidential signature isn’t holy water capable of washing a civil-rights violation clean. Who worked together to do it? Did officials privately agree to deny people their constitutional rights? If so, bring out the emails, not another smiling spokesman explaining that everybody meant well. I’ve heard more convincing excuses from children standing beside broken windows. Who thought federal judges were optional? Did anybody deliberately defy binding court orders on detention or deportation? If Miller was legally bound by an order and deliberately violated it, investigate. Courtrooms aren’t suggestion boxes, regardless of how many presidential portraits hang nearby. Who cooked the government books? Did anyone conspire to obstruct lawful government work through dishonesty? There’s a difference between hardball politics and rigging the game. Taxpayers didn’t hire a traveling three-card monte dealer to run the federal government. Who lied when the questions got serious? Did officials knowingly give material falsehoods to federal investigators? Political speeches can be stuffed with nonsense without automatically becoming crimes. But lies in a covered federal investigation are another matter. Suddenly the microphones are off, and somebody wants receipts. Who made the evidence disappear? Were records about families, arrests, or deportations altered or destroyed to obstruct investigation? Search the emails, preserve the files, and follow the missing documents. Government business shouldn’t vanish like socks in a dryer. Who leaned on the witnesses? Did anyone threaten employees, pressure subordinates to hide evidence, or coach witnesses into falsehoods? Let the officers, lawyers, and civil servants speak. If the policy was legal, honest testimony ought to be its best friend, not its worst nightmare. No, outrage isn’t evidence, and despicable politics aren’t automatically felonies. Criminal charges require proof of specific acts and intent; old allegations may face time limits. But neither should government power come with a lifetime pass against scrutiny. Investigate first. Let facts, not fury, decide the charges. That isn’t vengeance. It’s the minimum a republic owes its citizens. What barbarities might come next? Who knows what this political operator is capable of? The pattern deserves scrutiny: inflammatory rhetoric, punitive policy, and a determination to shrink the definition of an American. Related: The Politics of the Abyss: MAGA, Moral Rot, and the Struggle for the Future I won’t claim every other white man is Stephen Miller. That would be the kind of sweeping indictment I reject. But every American applauding this record while calling it law and order ought to examine what that applause supports. Cruelty doesn’t become citizenship merely because enough people cheer. Ordinary Americans have been warned repeatedly about surrendering their judgment and power to the powerful. Yet every generation produces citizens willing to call their neighbor’s suffering necessary, efficient, or patriotic. The question isn’t whether Miller might propose another cruelty. It’s how many respectable people will applaud, look away, or whisper that somebody probably had it coming. When subpoenas arrive, I want sworn answers, not sermons treating the Constitution as optional reading. Satan can keep his phone on. Washington has apparently extended his brother’s contract.
